findings.description: The `check` branch in `main` writes `fail` lines and `malformed` lines, then the summary, but never writes a `skip <short sha> merge commit` line for merge commits. `checkGitLog` does classify them as `skip` with reason `merge commit`, yet the loop only iterates for `c.verdict === 'fail'`, so the skipped commits reach neither stdout nor stderr. The merge-only CLI test (`a stream of only merge commits exits 0`) asserts only the `checked 2: ... 2 skipped` summary line, so it does not catch the omission. Users reading the output cannot see which merge commits were skipped, and a consumer that expects the specified ordered lines will misparse the output. The PR description says this is a known gap to be fixed before merge, but the diff as submitted still violates the output contract.
findings.title: Check output drops the merge-commit skip lines

citations.citation: Check CLI output and safe header formatting

evidence.explanation: Criterion 4802871 requires stdout to contain skipped-merge lines `skip <short sha> merge commit` between the malformed lines and the summary. The loop at src/cli.ts[385-388] emits only failing commits, so skipped merges are silently absent. src/check.ts[59] produces the skip verdict that the CLI then discards, and the merge-only test at tests/cli.test.ts[834-838] checks only the summary count, so it passes without the required lines. Criterion 4802873 also expects the merge-only case to be covered, and that test does not verify the output lines.

findings.description: `checkGitLog()` treats `message.conventional` as a pass, although `parseCommit()` computes that value after trimming the header's leading whitespace. A message such as `  feat: x` therefore passes and produces exit code 0 even though its untrimmed header does not match the grammar the command is meant to check.
findings.title: Malformed headers pass the commit check

findings.description: The new `check` argument-error branch interpolates `rest[0]` directly into stderr rather than escaping it with `oneLine()`. If an unexpected argument contains a newline or terminal control character, the diagnostic prints that character before the command returns exit code 2.
findings.title: Invalid options can forge error lines

evidence.explanation: The new branch receives the raw argv value and writes it directly to stderr, whereas the helper used for untrusted check output escapes controls and separators.

findings.description: `oneLine()` escapes controls and format characters but leaves invisible characters in other Unicode categories unchanged. A failing header such as `feat<U+034F>: x` retains the combining grapheme joiner in terminal output, so the displayed header can appear to be the valid `feat: x` while the checker reports a failure.
findings.title: Invisible characters hide in failed headers

findings.description: The third process exception lets an interactive agent commit, push and open a pull request after giving the gate report, without requiring the human to acknowledge it. When the human asks for the task before seeing that report, the agent can perform those actions immediately after presenting it, despite Gate 4 requiring the human to read it first.
findings.title: Agents can publish before gate review

citations.citation:
- Third exception (Day 12): when the human asks for it in the conversation, for one named task,
  an interactive agent may make that task's first commit, push its branch and open its pull
  request (draft or ready, as asked). Before committing, the agent gives the gate report and
  states the branch, the files and the pull request title and body; the request covers that one
  task and does not carry over. Limits: `npm run check` passes; never on `main`; new commits
  only, never an amend, force-push or rebase; the pull request body follows the ticket rules
  (`Closes #N`). Merging stays human, and so do labels and every other trigger.
